steps.what: Read market conditions for the name.
Price securities or commodities from those conditions.
Write that price onto the order ticket.

tasks.design: Market conditions for the name sit on a {BI} view from the market terminal ({OTHER}). The agent prices the security or the commodity. That price is written onto the order ticket and signed before anyone can send it. The view does not set the price.
tasks.previous_blocker: The price was a number in a notebook, with the conditions on another screen.
tasks.enabler_now: The conditions can be on one view. Setting the price from them is still the agent's judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A thin market, a wide spread, or a client limit can make the screen's mid price the wrong one.
tasks.human_edge: The agent sets the price. The conditions sheet is not a pricing model and must not become one.

ambition.what: Price a small security from the same conditions sheet, including names too small to reconstruct by hand.

tasks.altitude: The agent still sets every price. Hunting the conditions leaves the task.

reach.task: set a premium from the conditions on the file
reach.learn: which input is a fact and which number the person must set

evidence.claim: Showing market conditions is a dashboard. The job digest does not treat pricing a security as a sum a model may finish.
The priced ticket is an order record. The job digest says order-related calls and messages are kept for five years, and up to seven, even when no trade follows.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task sets the price. Sending the order is another task, and it may use only this signed price.

Fields: instrument id, quote, as-of, factor names, price, size. Conditions come from the terminal and the factor log. The agent types the price. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The terminal already shows the quote. The build gathers conditions. It does not add an automated pricer.
The signature is the price version. Any edit voids it. No seller score is stored.
unknowns: Whether commodities and securities share one conditions sheet on this desk.
What spread the agent is allowed to set.
research_questions: What share of prices is still a notebook number?
How often does the signed price change before the send?

already_counted.description: The agent still sets the price.
The agent still writes it onto the ticket.

incremental.description: Keep the conditions view mapped to the terminal.

approvals.approved_version: price-mark v1: instrument, conditions-as-of, price, size

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If conditions are incomplete, the agent still prices from the terminal by hand and the sheet saves only the names it covers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Buy or sell a financial derivative.

steps.what: Show the derivative terms and the client limit.
Purchase or sell financial derivatives for customers.
Approve the derivative ticket before the send.

tasks.design: Derivative terms and the client limit are on one {CRM} screen, with the quote from the market terminal ({OTHER}). The agent purchases or sells with the customer and approves the ticket version. No ticket leaves without that approval. The message is stored in {DOCS}. The screen does not choose the derivative.
tasks.previous_blocker: Terms, limit and ticket were three screens, so a send could leave with the wrong expiry.
tasks.enabler_now: The terms are fields. Showing them beside the limit stops a blind send. It does not decide the trade.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this customer should hold the derivative, and at what size, is the agent's decision.
tasks.human_edge: The agent makes the purchase or the sale and signs the ticket. A term sheet is not that decision.
tasks.altitude: The derivative decision stays with the agent. A mismatched ticket is harder to send.

reach.task: bind a cover only after the limit and the terms match
reach.learn: which field, once changed, must void the approval

evidence.claim: Showing derivative terms next to a client limit is a record. The decision stays with the agent.

The job digest says securities advice stays with the person, and advising staff need a diploma. A draft is not the advice. The job digest says order-related calls and messages are kept for five years, and up to seven, even when no trade follows. The job digest says life and health pricing and consumer creditworthiness are the high-risk cases. This ticket is neither, and it is still not automatic.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The task is the derivative conversation and the ticket approval. A later venue reject is handled as an order reject, not here.

Fields: derivative id, expiry, strike, side, size, premium, client id, limit. Terms are shown from the product record. The agent confirms side and size against the limit. A size above the limit cannot be approved. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The {CRM} already holds the client limit. The build shows the terms beside it and blocks an approval over the limit. It does not add a trading engine.
The approval is the version that may be sent. Any edit voids it. No seller score is stored.
unknowns: Whether these customers may trade derivatives under the firm's permissions.
Whether the venue needs a second signature above a size.
research_questions: What share of derivative tickets is stopped by the client limit?
How often does the expiry change after the conversation?

already_counted.description: The agent still deals with the customer.
The agent still approves the ticket.

incremental.description: Keep the derivative term fields and the limit check current.

approvals.approved_version: derivative-ticket v1: derivative-id, expiry, strike, side, size, client-id, limit

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the customer still decides on a long call and the terms are often incomplete, the screen saves the limit check and not the conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The agent keeps the price and the derivative decision. The market picture is assembled before either one.
reach: Insurance sales agent: price a risk from conditions on the file, and learn which condition the person must still judge.
Travel agent: confirm a fare against published conditions before the customer is committed.
skills_to_grow: Write a price as a version that a later edit voids.
Refuse a derivative ticket that does not match the client's limit.
role.ambitious_version: A small security is priced from the same market conditions as a large one, and a derivative is sent only in the version the agent signed.
